input: Take a CPR and first aid certification course

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: CPR/first aid courses vary widely — basic adult CPR, pediatric CPR, BLS for healthcare providers, full first aid, or AED training. Knowing which certifications are needed determines which course to enroll in.

Whether this is for personal knowledge, a job requirement, or for a specific role (e.g., teacher, coach, parent) affects which certifying body (Red Cross, AHA, ASHI, etc.) and which course level is appropriate.
Whether the user prefers in-person, online-only, or a blended (online + hands-on skills test) format will narrow down which providers and locations are viable options.
Courses range from free community offerings to $100+ paid sessions. Budget determines which providers to consider and whether employer reimbursement is a factor.
The user's location determines which local classes, training centers, or hospitals offer sessions, and how far they are willing to travel affects scheduling.

Some employers or organizations require certification from a specific body (e.g., American Heart Association vs. Red Cross). Knowing if there is a required certifying organization ensures the certificate will actually be accepted.
Certification cards typically expire in 1-2 years. Knowing whether the user wants the longest validity period, or values a faster completion time, shapes which course format to prioritize.

gold.taskTitle: Get CPR and First Aid Certified
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to complete a CPR and first aid certification course and earn a recognized credential.

questions.title: Which specific certifications do you need to earn?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user needs basic CPR only, full first aid, pediatric CPR, AED training, BLS for healthcare providers, or a combination — since each maps to a different course.

questions.title: Is this for a job, role, or personal preparedness?
questions.description: Determine the reason behind getting certified — a workplace mandate, a volunteer role, a sport coaching position, or general personal readiness — as this affects which certifying body's credential is needed.

questions.title: Do you prefer in-person, online, or a blended class format?
questions.description: Establish whether the user wants a fully in-person hands-on class, a fully online course, or a blended option (online learning + in-person skills check) to filter available providers.

questions.title: What is your budget for the course and materials?
questions.description: Identify how much the user is willing to spend, from free community courses to paid professional training sessions, and whether employer reimbursement is available.

questions.title: What city or area are you located in?
questions.description: Pinpoint the user's location to identify nearby training centers, hospitals, fire stations, or community organizations that offer classes.

questions.title: Does a specific certifying organization need to issue your card?
questions.description: Find out if the user's employer, school, or organization requires certification from a particular body such as the American Heart Association or American Red Cross.

questions.title: How soon do you need to complete the certification?
questions.description: Determine the user's deadline or urgency — whether they need it within days, weeks, or have a flexible timeline — to prioritize course availability and scheduling.
